messages:
Nadia (People Ops): Quick note: mid-year cycle timeline is live. Key anchors are in the doc: self-reflections close 2026-07-01, manager summaries due 2026-07-08, calibration panels 2026-07-12 -> 07-14, final locks 2026-07-16. Please skim the "how panels run" section before submitting. Link: https://go/redwood/mid-year-2026 :sparkles:

Ethan (People Ops): New additions this cycle: concise "evidence bullets" (3 lines max) and an explicit manager checklist for pre-panel prep. Also we've added a short template for manager 1:1s post-calibration.

Rina (Eng Manager): Two Qs: 1) Are we required to upload anonymized peer notes? 2) If a report is on LOA, do we auto-defer?

Nadia (People Ops): 1) Peer notes are optional but encouraged for cross-team contributors. They get aggregated and anonymized. 2) For LOA >10 days during the cycle, managers can request a deferral via the ext form; People Ops approves within 48 hrs. Max auto-deferral is 21 days without exec sign-off.

Ola (IC): Any guidance on writing the one-line achievement in the self-reflection? I always over-write.

Ethan (People Ops): Try: "Context + Action + Outcome (metric or qualitative)". Example: "Led rollout of model caching layer; reduced median response lat by 35% and cut infra costs ~7%." Keep it to one line and one measurable result if possible.

Marcus (Director): For calibration panels: who serves as the panel lead and how are disagreements escalated?

Nadia (People Ops): Panel lead is typically a director-level rep or senior manager from another org. Escalation flow: panel discussion -> if panel majority differs by more than one band from manager rec, panel lead flags for a 20-min reconvene. If unresolved, Calibration Chair (exec sponsor) makes final call. We try to keep escalations minimal.

Rina (Eng Manager): Is there an appeals window after ratings? Last cycle people asked about this.

Ethan (People Ops): Yes: 10 business days post-release. Appeals must include new evidence or point to process issues. People Ops triages and routes to Calibration Chair.

Ola (IC): Will managers be required to have a 1:1 within X days after ratings? I want to know when to expect feedback.

Nadia (People Ops): Managers must hold a 1:1 within 3 business days after ratings lock to share outcomes and a short development plan. There's a paste-ready manager script in the doc if helpful.

SchedulerBot: Reminder: manager summaries due in 7 days for teams with >3 directs. Upload link: https://go/redwood/manager-upload :bell:

Rina (Eng Manager): Can People Ops paste the manager invite blurb we can reuse? Makes scheduling faster.

Ethan (People Ops): Paste this into invites: "Calibration panel: please review attached anonymized pre-reads before the session. Bring 2 talking points per review (impact, dev plan). We'll timebox to 10-12 mins per person. Anchors: https://go/redwood/mid-year-2026"

Marcus (Director): One policy ask: managers should not include comp rationale in initial manager summaries. That goes into the post-calibration comp worksheet handled by People Ops & Finance.

Ola (IC): If I'm traveling and miss the 1:1 window, how will I get my feedback?

Nadia (People Ops): Managers should record a short voice memo or schedule a follow-up within the next 5 business days. If you need an asynchronous alternative, flag it in the exception form and People Ops will coordinate.

Rina (Eng Manager): Last: any recommended size for panels? I've been part of 7-person panels before and they drag.

Ethan (People Ops): Recommended default: 4-5 people (3 managers from different teams + 1 senior IC + 1 People Ops rep). For high volume orgs, we run parallel panels. Keep panels small and evidence-focused.

Nadia (People Ops): Thanks everyone. If you have edge cases (international comp cycles, pending offers), DM People Ops so we can align timing with Recruiting/Finance. Final reminder: read the anchors doc before panels.
